To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the tecto-ventral mesencephalic endogenous opioid peptide disinhibitory pathway modulates the nigro-tecto-dorsal midbrain inhibitory links that are involved in the organisation of panic-like behaviour.
the endogenous opioid peptides in the dlSC, dlPAG and SNpr are involved in the modulation of panic-like behaviour.

the interaction between the opioidergic and GAB-ergic mechanisms in the continuum comprised of the dlSC and dlPAG modulates the escape behaviour threshold elicited by electrical stimulation of the dorsal midbrain.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the chemical neuroanatomy of the endogenous opioid peptide systems involved in the control of innate fear-induced behaviour and the psychopharmacology of the endogenous opioids in the control of the innate fear-induced behaviours.
the chemical neuroanatomical organisation of the endogenous opioidergic system and its functional role in the modulation of panic-like behaviour.

the study of the chemical neuroanatomy of the midbrain and its role in the control of innate fear-induced behaviours, with a special focus on the interaction between the endogenous opioid peptide and GABA neurotransmitter systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the opioidergic systems in the midbrain and substantia nigra, and the interaction between them, are involved in the regulation of panic-like behaviour.
endogenous opioid peptides in the dorsal mid-brain and substantia nigra, acting on κ-opioid receptors, modulate the innate fear-induced escape responses elicited by tectal electrical stimulation.

the tectal opioid system is involved in the regulation of the escape behaviour threshold, probably through a modulation of the GABAergic nigrotectal neurons that inhibit the tectal neurons that control the escape behaviour threshold.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the opioidergic system is involved in the regulation of the escape behaviour threshold in the continuum comprised of the dlSC and dlPAG.
endogenous opioid peptides, acting at κ-opioid receptors in the dlSC and dlPAG, exert a disinhibitory effect on nigro-tecto-mesencephalic neurons and, in this way, modulate panic-like behaviour.

the opioidergic system, through the activation of κ-opioid receptors, is involved in the modulation of fear-related responses, and that the opioidergic modulation of the nigro-tectum circuitry is a key mechanism for the control of panic attacks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the opioidergic and GABAmimetic systems in the midbrain are part of the neuroanatomical substratum for the control of innate fear-related responses and panic-like behaviour.

the endogenous opioid peptide system in the midbrain tecta and SNpr is a key component of the neuroanatomical substrates involved in the control of innate fear responses and that it may be a target for the development of novel pharmacological strategies in the management of fear-related disorders.

opioidergic neurotransmission in the dlSC and dlPAG modulates innate fear-related responses, and that the nigro-tecto-dorsal midbrain pathway may be an important component in the control of the emotional response to aversive stimuli.
